oligos.developer: Bayer AG and Ionis Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (joint sponsors of the trials)
oligos.max_phase: Phase 1 in this source (three phase I studies: first-in-human, Japanese, Chinese)
oligos.sequence_locus: NOT_REPORTED - stated to share the sequence of BAY 2306001 (ISIS 416858), but that sequence is not printed here or in S14/S15

measurements.verbatim_quote: Maximum mean ± SD aPTT prolongation was observed on day 92 with 46.1 ± 30.6 seconds in the 200 mg group, 49.4 ± 37.5 seconds in the 300 mg group, and 36.0 ± 25.4 seconds in the placebo group.
measurements.notes: HAZARD FOR REVIEWERS: the placebo arm's own day-92 aPTT is 36.0 s against a 27.4 s baseline, and every arm carries an enormous SD (25-38 s). measurements.system_model: Patients undergoing elective primary unilateral total knee arthroplasty; phase 2 open-label randomised parallel-group adaptive trial NCT01713361 (FXI-ASO TKA), 19 centres in 5 countries
measurements.timepoint: All events during study treatment and follow-up until day 136 (safety population)
measurements.exposure_duration: 36 days pre-operative dosing plus post-operative doses; follow-up to day 136
measurements.control_description: Enoxaparin 40 mg once-daily comparator arm, N = 72 (there is no placebo arm in this trial)
measurements.effect_vs_control: Arm: FXI-ASO 200 mg. Risk difference vs enoxaparin for the principal safety outcome was −6 (−12 to 1) for 200 mg and −6 (−13 to 2) for 300 mg; Fisher exact P = 0.09 and 0.16 respectively - i.e. numerically LESS bleeding on the ASO, not significantly so.
measurements.severity_stated_by_source: The rate of major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding was lower with the 300-mg dose regimen than with enoxaparin (3% vs 8%), a difference that did not reach statistical significance.
measurements.source_locus: Table 2 (Efficacy and Safety Outcomes), safety block, row 'Principal safety outcome: major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding'
measurements.verbatim_quote: Principal safety outcome: major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding — no. (% [95% CI]) | 4 (3 [1 to 7]) | 2 (3 [<1 to 9]) | 6 (8 [3 to 17])
measurements.notes: Table row rendered cell-by-cell in printed column order: FXI-ASO 200 mg (N=144) | FXI-ASO 300 mg (N=77) | enoxaparin 40 mg (N=72). The em dash and the footnote marker are the source's. Note the source's own caveat: 'the strength of our conclusion regarding bleeding is limited by the modest sample size'. Transfusion rates are high in all arms because this is major orthopaedic surgery, so the transfusion row is a poor bleeding proxy on its own.

measurements.notes: Geometric mean with geometric CV% in parentheses, expressed as a RATIO to that participant's own baseline - not seconds. Value assigned by position in the printed sentence (order: Caucasian, Japanese, Chinese; then 40, 80, 120 mg). measurements.system_model: Healthy volunteers in three phase I studies (first-in-human/Caucasian, Japanese, Chinese), pooled as the interethnic pharmacodynamic analysis set (iPDS)
measurements.timepoint: Emax - minimum ratio to baseline after a single injection; maximum inhibition mainly between Day 15 and Day 30
measurements.exposure_duration: single dose, followed for up to 149 days
measurements.control_description: Same group's own baseline FXI activity in U/mL (Table 1); 'Injection of placebo had no effect on FXI activity (Figure 2).'
measurements.effect_vs_control: Ethnicity: Caucasian. Dose-dependent fall: at 120 mg FXI activity reaches 0.26-0.36 of baseline. This is the on-target axis that the aPTT row must be read against.
measurements.severity_stated_by_source: NOT_REPORTED
measurements.source_locus: Results, section 'PD', first paragraph (FXI activity); values also plotted in Figure 2
measurements.verbatim_quote: Geometric mean (CV, %) of the minimum ratios to baseline of FXI activity in Caucasian, Japanese, and Chinese participants with fesomersen 40 mg were 0.596 (12.9), 0.480 (35.2), and 0.570 (27.3), respectively; with fesomersen 80 mg were 0.381 (41.4), 0.369 (21.6), and 0.362 (28.2), respectively; and with fesomersen 120 mg were 0.260 (21.1), 0.360 (71.7), and 0.268 (73.5), respectively.

extraction_notes:
SCOPE AND WHAT THIS BUNDLE CONTRIBUTES
fxi-pkk-clinical covers on-target FXI and prekallikrein knockdown across four modalities and four species: unconjugated 2'-MOE ASO (IONIS-FXIRx / ISIS 416858 / BAY2306001, S14 + S15), a baboon-specific FXI MOE gapmer (S16), the GalNAc-conjugated version of the same FXI sequence (fesomersen, S17), a prekallikrein MOE gapmer (IONIS-PKKRx, S18), a GalNAc-siRNA against FXI (RBD4059, S38) and an LNP siRNA against fibrinogen (siFibrinogen, S51). Every compound here is DESIGNED to alter coagulation, so most rows carry on_target_effect true; the interesting rows are the ones where that flag is false.

QUOTE VERIFICATION - READ THIS BEFORE TRUSTING A verbatim_quote
All 176 measurement rows were machine-verified: every verbatim_quote is a literal substring (after whitespace normalisation) of the flattened text of its own source file. Zero rows failed.
The flattening was done with a custom ElementTree walker over the JATS XML; the flattened copies used for verification are in the session scratchpad, and the authoritative files are the local_path values in "sources".
CONVENTION FOR TABLE ROWS: 73 of the 176 quotes are TABLE ROWS. A JATS table row has no single run of prose to copy, so it is rendered cell-by-cell, in printed column order, separated by " | ". The cell CONTENTS are verbatim; the pipe characters and the column order are the rendering. Every such row's notes field states the column order explicitly, so a reviewer can map value to arm without guessing. A second check parsed the raw XML and confirmed every individual cell string appears there; the only divergences were whitespace around superscript footnote markers (e.g. the source's "Major bleeding — no. (% [95% CI])" followed by a superscript paragraph mark), which the flattener joins and the XML itext separates. No cell value differed.
DERIVED COUNTS: 10 rows carry an explicit "DERIVED-COUNT FLAG" in notes. These are zero-event or single-event bleeding counts where the source states the fact in prose ("No other bleeding events were reported", "one Caucasian participant ... reported an AE of mild epistaxis") and the n_of_N form was constructed from that prose plus the group size stated elsewhere in the same source. THE S18 ATTRIBUTION SPLIT - THE MOST IMPORTANT THING IN THIS BUNDLE
S18 is the only source in the union that separates, within one compound, the 2'-MOE phosphorothioate CLASS effect on aPTT from genuine on-target contact-pathway depletion. Both are captured, with opposite flags:
 - CLASS EFFECT (on_target_effect FALSE, unintended_toxicity TRUE): in cynomolgus monkeys the aPTT was prolonged "by 2.5 s compared with baseline" at 12 mg/kg/week and "by ~13 s" at 40 mg/kg/week, peaking 4-8 h post-dose and back to baseline by 24 h. The source states this "is directly related to the ASO plasma concentration" and "indicates that the observed effects on aPTT were not related to the pharmacologic reduction of PKK". In humans the same effect appears as "slight, transient mean increases in aPTT [that] were not clinically significant", never crossing the upper limit of normal.
 - ON-TARGET (on_target_effect TRUE): "There were no lasting effects on aPTT associated with the pharmacologic reduction of PKK" in monkeys, despite 85% plasma PKK depletion; and in humans the contact-pathway effect was detectable ONLY on a bespoke PKK-sensitised assay ("The activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) assay was optimized ... to account for pharmacological reduction of plasma PKK", APTT-A reagent, 60 s incubation), where "dose-dependent increases in the optimized aPTT were observed in the 300 and 400 mg cohort on days 23 and 50".
DIAGNOSTIC RULE this yields for the rest of the dataset: a 4-8 h aPTT peak that resolves by 24 h and scales with plasma ASO concentration is chemistry, not pharmacology. Every aPTT row in this bundle that peaks on the order of days-to-weeks (S14 day 92, S15 perioperative, S17 day 15-30, S38 day 15 mouse / day 29 monkey) is therefore on-target, and is flagged that way. Note also that 92-94% prekallikrein depletion did NOT push the standard aPTT above the upper limit of normal - the standard aPTT is a poor target-engagement assay for a contact-system drug, and pooling "aPTT" across sources without preserving the assay variant would conflate two different measurements.

INTERPRETATION HAZARDS A REVIEWER MUST KNOW
 - S14 aPTT values are heparin-contaminated. Every patient was on haemodialysis and 84.6-93.3% received unfractionated heparin for circuit anticoagulation. The placebo arm's own day-92 aPTT is 36.0 s against a 27.4 s baseline, and every arm's SD is 25-38 s - larger than the mean effect. The IONIS-FXIRx signal is only interpretable as the INCREMENT over the concurrent placebo arm (+10.1 s at 200 mg, +13.4 s at 300 mg), never as an absolute clotting time. Do not pool these seconds with the healthy-volunteer aPTTs in S17.
 - S14 arms are not balanced for the thrombotic endpoint at baseline: before week 6, category >=3 circuit clotting ran at 73.7% in the 200 mg arm but 39.8% in the 300 mg arm and 51.6% on placebo. The within-patient difference analysis partly handles this; the raw proportions do not.
 - S15 has NO placebo arm. Its comparator is enoxaparin 40 mg, an active anticoagulant. "Less bleeding than enoxaparin" is not "no bleeding". Efficacy Ns (134/71/69, per-protocol) differ from safety Ns (144/77/72, safety population) and the rows carry the right one for each outcome.
 - S17 cohorts are tiny (n=4-12 per ethnicity per dose) and baseline-imbalanced by design: Japanese participants have systematically higher baseline aPTT and lower baseline FXI activity than Caucasian or Chinese participants. This is why the source works in ratio-to-baseline. The 120 mg Japanese and Chinese FXI-activity CVs are 71.7% and 73.5%. The 80 mg Caucasian aPTT ratio (1.414) exceeds the 120 mg Caucasian ratio (1.397), so dose-response is not strictly monotonic at the top of the range.
 - S16's thrombosis endpoint is measured as 111In-labelled PLATELET accumulation in an AV-shunt device. This is thrombus mass, not a platelet count, and the source ties it explicitly to upstream thrombin generation. It is filed under thrombotic_outcome, not platelet_coag_crosstalk, and the notes say so on every affected row.
 - S16's most striking finding is a non-linearity that matters for dose-setting: a 30% fall in plasma FXI produced a 60-75% fall in peak thrombin generation, and below 50% FXI, thrombin generation was "virtually abolished". A modest aPTT change can therefore accompany a large functional anticoagulant effect.
 - S38 has an unexplained animal death: "Due to the death of 1 test animal, the 9 mg/kg group has n = 5 from day 29." No cause is given and the source does not discuss it. Captured in the notes of the affected monkey rows. The same source cites GLP NOAELs of 600 mg/kg (mouse) and 400 mg/kg (monkey) but marks them "unpublished data included in the IND documentation" - not extracted, because the underlying study is not accessible.
 - S38 also has an internal timing mismatch it does not comment on: maximum mouse APTT prolongation is at day 15 but maximum FXI-activity reduction is at day 29.
 - S51 is abstract-only and its licence is unresolved. Do not redistribute its text.

ABSENCE ROWS (measured nulls) VERSUS SILENCE
This bundle is unusually rich in measured nulls and they are the point, not filler: FXI/PKK inhibition is supposed to dissociate thrombosis from haemostasis, so a credible null is the primary safety evidence. 28 rows carry effect_direction "no_change", and every one of them quotes a source sentence reporting that the endpoint WAS measured and found unchanged. The strongest are: the baboon bleeding time (4.0 +/- 0.3 min treated vs 3.9 +/- 0.3 min naive, p > 0.5, measured in the same animals whose aPTT was prolonged and whose thrombin generation was abolished); the RBD4059 mouse tail bleed, which is positive-control validated because enoxaparin in the same experiment DID prolong bleeding (P < 0.05); and the S51 haemostasis null, which was measured under an active haemorrhagic-shock challenge rather than at rest. Nulls that are only "data not shown" (S15 PT ratio and factors VIII/IX/XII; S16 PT) are entered with readout_value NOT_REPORTED and say so.
Where a source simply never mentions an endpoint, no row was written; the absent endpoints for this bundle are listed in refused_rows.
